correctness.rationale: At a positive equilibrium, direct differentiation gives the Jacobian with trace 1-rx+A and determinant (1-rx)A+B. The predator-nullcline derivative satisfies g'(y)=x(1-A)/y and the prey-nullcline derivative satisfies B=-r y f'(y), so det(I-J)=r y(g'-f')=-r y H'. In an exactly-two-root regime a simple lower root crosses H from negative to positive, hence H'>0 and p(1)<0. A monic real quadratic with p(1)<0 has a real root above 1. If rx<=2, p(-1)=(2-rx)(1+A)+B>0, placing the other real root in (-1,1). The source examples were independently replayed from the printed map.

value.rationale: The result directly addresses an open analytical point identified by the motivating article. It converts a difficult-looking pair of Jury inequalities into a single exact nullcline-slope identity, proving instability for every transverse lower coexistence equilibrium and giving a clean saddle criterion. This explains both source examples with one structural mechanism and sharpens interpretation of the bistable extinction-coexistence threshold without requiring a global basin theorem.
